Write a list of participant triplet data frames to a CSV file

write_triplet_list.Rd

Converts a named or unnamed list of per-participant triplet data frames – the package's standard Center/Left/Right/ Answer/worker_id shape, e.g. icon_triplets – into a single combined CSV file, one row per trial. Counterpart to write_embedding_list, for triplet data rather than fitted embeddings; the result round-trips through get.combined (eflag = FALSE).

Usage

write_triplet_list(triplet_list, file)

Arguments

triplet_list

A list of data frames, one per participant, each with its own worker_id column (the format find_frequent_triplets and assign_validation_from_frequency also expect).

file

Path to the output CSV file. The parent directory must already exist.

Value

The output file path, invisibly.

Details

Participants' data frames are combined with bind_rows rather than rbind(), so they don't need to share identical columns or column order – a real possibility for legacy data assembled from several sources (e.g. after splitting off a held-out subset of participants, or combining data read in separate batches).

Output format

The CSV has one row per trial, with every column present in any element of triplet_list (participants whose own data frame is missing a column some other participant has get NA in that column, via bind_rows – see Details). Unlike write_embedding_list, worker_id is read directly from each data frame's own worker_id column, not from names(triplet_list) – the list itself need not be named (most of this package's own triplet lists, e.g. those built by read_raw_data, are not).

See also

write_embedding_list for the embedding-list analogue; get.combined to read the result back in.

Examples

out <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
write_triplet_list(icon_triplets, out)

# Read back and reconstruct the named list
triplet_list <- get.combined(out, eflag = FALSE)
names(triplet_list)
#> [1] "3n7ggxph" "b5wma4no" "d8mmm1qn" "jn7bbjc0" "pbby694o" "sc2xbd6w"
